title: On‑Prem K8s rollback & chaos simulation notes
content:
Context and purpose:
This doc captures planned rollback simulations and chaos tests for on‑prem Kubernetes clusters (bare metal + vSphere). The goal is to exercise the exact sequences customers will require during upgrades or hardware failures so our Terraform modules, bootstrap hooks, and runbooks behave predictably. This is intentionally pragmatic: short checklists, commands, and telemetry targets.

Scope and constraints:
- Clusters: small test clusters (3 control-plane / 3 worker) and a 5× production‑like cluster (control-plane HA + mixed CPU/GPU workers).
- Platforms: bare metal PXE boot + IPMI; vSphere VMs from template + cloud‑init.
- State backends: Terraform state in S3 (minio) for test infra; customer templates use S3/GCS or onprem object store.
- Storage: we test both CSI (vSphere CSI, local‑lv) and localPersistentVolume use cases.
- Backups: Velero (S3 compatible) for cluster backup/restore scenarios.

High‑level simulation matrix (to run against each test cluster):
1) Upgrade path failure simulations
   - in‑place kubeadm/k8s control-plane upgrade interrupted mid‑flight (power cycle one control-plane)
   - worker node kubelet crash during node image upgrade (docker/containerd restart loop)
   - terraform apply with module breaking change then rollback (taint + recreate)
2) Infrastructure failures
   - vSphere vCenter network partition (simulate via iptables on VMs)
   - bare metal switch port flaps (power cycle NIC / simulate packet loss with tc)
   - storage array latency spike (fio on storage nodes)
3) Data plane chaos
   - eviction pressure: kill kube-proxy/iptables on 1–2 nodes
   - API server GC pause (simulate long GC by resource storm)
4) Full cluster evacuation & restore
   - Velero backup, destroy cluster, restore to new hardware/VC

Test case detail: interrupted control-plane upgrade (example)
- Preconditions:
  - cluster running v1.25 -> target v1.26 (test lab channel patched images)
  - 3 control-plane nodes (cp-0..cp-2), kubeadm upgrade flow validated in staging
  - terraform state snapshot saved (terraform state pull > state.snap)
- Steps:
  1. Start kubeadm upgrade on cp-0: kubeadm upgrade apply v1.26.x --force
  2. After kubelet restarts and new kube-apiserver pods are scheduled, manually power‑off cp-1 (IPMI or vSphere poweroff)
  3. Wait 30–90s for control-plane quorum change and observe API errors from clients
  4. Reboot cp-1, check kube-apiserver logs for data migrations/errors
  5. If control-plane does not recover within SLO (5m), run rollback plan:
     - If using kubeadm rollback path exists: follow documented kubeadm rollback (only if tested)
     - Otherwise restore etcd snapshot (Velero does not back up etcd—use etcdctl snapshot stored in S3/minio)
- Observables / telemetry to capture:
  - API error rates (429/5xx) and p99 latencies
  - etcd leader election frequency and commit latency
  - Terraform plan/apply diff before/after (report)

Terraform module idempotency checks (notes)
- Run sequence: terraform init -> plan -> apply -> plan (should be no changes).
- For interrupted apply: simulate by killing terraform process mid‑apply; then run terraform apply again and verify drift is reconciled.
- Ensure modules expose:
  - safe_create_only: bool (default false) for resources that cannot be safely replaced (e.g., physical BMC assignments)
  - lifecycle ignore_changes for fields updated by vSphere provider (like bios settings)
- State backend quirks: when using local backend in labs, do an explicit state backup before destructive exercises (cp-mirror: aws s3 cp state.tfstate state.snap)

vSphere specific test notes
- Snapshot vs clone behavior: avoid snapshots for cluster nodes that use local PVs; snapshots can corrupt file handles on local devices.
- vCenter partition simulation: use firewall rules on ESXi management network or toggle VMWare Tools heartbeat to test HA restart paths.
- VM hardware upgrade rollback: change VM hardware version in a test template, boot one node with upgraded hardware, then attempt to revert to previous template (expect kernel/driver issues).
- Recommended check: disable vSphere change tracking during large upgrades to avoid churn in provider diffs.

Bare metal specific test notes
- PXE + iPXE chain changes: test a two-stage bootflow rollback — have factory images available and validate reimaging time (target < 20m per node).
- IPMI failure mode: simulate BMC unreachable by blocking UDP/623; confirm on-call runbook for manual console access.
- Local NVMe/drive replacement: test hot-swap behavior and re-provision flow (terraform taint node resource -> recreate node).

Velero backup/restore playbook (brief)
- Pretest: run velero install with restic for local PVs, run velero schedule create nightly-test --schedule='0 3 * * *'
- Backup flow: velero backup create preupgrade-YYYYMMDD --include-namespaces default,kube-system --wait
- Restore flow to new cluster: velero restore create --from-backup preupgrade-YYYYMMDD --wait; after restore, reattach PVs and run sanity e2e tests
- Known caveat: CRDs and cluster-scoped resources ordering can break restores — use hooks to reapply CRDs first.

Chaos experiments & tooling
- Use kube‑chaos (litmus) for pod eviction/network partition experiments. For infra-level faults use:
  - vSphere: use govc to disconnect hosts or poweroff VMs
  - Baremetal: ipmitool/chassis power cycle + tc for network disruption
  - Generic: run a small runner that executes `kubectl cordon/evict` + `systemctl stop kubelet` on target nodes via SSH
- Safety controls:
  - Always run in lab org & tag test clusters with `chaos:test=true` label
  - Global circuit breaker: if API errors > threshold (10% 5xx across cluster for 2m) abort automation and start recovery checklist

Rollbacks for Terraform-driven changes (recommended steps)
1. Pause automation pipelines (Circle/GitHub actions) to stop concurrent applies.
2. Run terraform plan against state snapshot to understand drift.
3. If resource replacement was started and failed, prefer a targeted `terraform apply -target=module.name.resource` to stabilize one resource at a time.
4. For resources that cannot be safely recreated (storage, BMC), use provider-level repair: reassign existing VM IDs in TF state with `terraform state rm` + `terraform import`
5. If state is corrupted: restore state.snap and re-run plan/apply in a staging namespace first

Runbook excerpt (quick checklist for on-call during failed upgrade):
- Triage: check cluster health (kubectl get componentstatus && kubectl get nodes)
- Check etcd health: ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl endpoint status --cluster
- If control-plane down: attempt to SSH to leader cp node, check kubelet, container runtime, and kube-apiserver logs
- If nodes unreachable: test network connectivity to BMC and host, run `ipmitool chassis status` (baremetal) or `govc vm.power` (vSphere)
- Evacuation: cordon + drain non-critical workers, scale statefulsets down with predrain hooks, snapshot PVs where possible
- Restore path: Velero restore for workloads, etcd snapshot restore for cluster state, terraform apply for infra reconciliation

Metrics and SLOs for simulation acceptance criteria
- Control-plane recovery time: target < 5m for single node failure, < 15m for two nodes (lab targets)
- No data loss for stateful apps after restore (validated by end‑to‑end job run)
- Terraform idempotence: consecutive apply results in 0 resource changes in >90% of runs
- Velero restore success rate >95% for cluster-scoped components in test runs

Open questions / TODOs
- Validate kubeadm rollback feasibility across versions we support — add matrix and results
- Add automated harness to snapshot Terraform state before every major apply in labs
- Decide a canonical tool for simulating vCenter network partitions (govc + vSphere firewall vs injecting iptables rules inside ESXi management VM)
- Document exact etcd snapshot retention policy and object store lifecycle in private deployments docs

Appendix: quick commands cheat sheet
- cordon & drain: kubectl cordon NODE && kubectl drain NODE --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
- etcd snapshot: ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl snapshot save /tmp/etcd-$(date -I).db --endpoints=https://127.0.0.1:2379 --cert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.crt --key=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.key --cacert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/ca.crt
- terraform safe reapply: terraform apply -auto-approve -target=module.network -state=state.snap
- vSphere power cycle via govc: govc vm.power -host vcenter-host -off vm-name; govc vm.power -on vm-name

Notes to self: keep experiments small & repeatable. Capture full logs to S3/minio and tag runs with git sha + test id. Will put scripts into repo: github.com/redwood-inference/private-deploy-tests (WIP).
